pending_commit.commit_message: CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: Add BT splitter BT splitter is a simple BT device virtualization layer that allows bluez to share the chip with a userspace stack. The userspace stack handles all LE and bluez - EDR. This code hides LE capabilities of the chip from bluez, and thus no more changes to bluez are likely to be needed. The userspace stack is built aware of this splitter and acts accordingly (not using EDR), though this is not necessarily required, as the userspace stack can be shown an LE-only chip too. We choose not to do that as we control that stack already and there is thus no need for this. There are improvements that can be made (like seeing if there are separate LE buffers before stealing EDR bufers), which we'll address soon. The way userspace connects to this: * open /dev/hci_splitter and treat it asn an hci device * when opened a RESET command complete packet will be read * it will have the "number of comands" value set to 0 or 1 * 0 if chip i snot yet ready (and stack will wait as per spec) * 1 if chip is ready * if userspace dies, chip is reset (as no state exosts to restore it back to normalcy). * if bluez resets chip or otherwise shuts it down, another command complete event is sent as a reset (as chip is indeed reset) with "number of commands" value set to zero TEST=verified bluez remains functional and does not see any LE features with splitter on BUG=35775020 Change-Id: I2ad520b26bf7a35dc98ed2548c936734afd98f39 Signed-off-by: Dmitry Grinberg <dmitrygr@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1551945 Commit-Ready: Sonny Sasaka <sonnysasaka@chromium.org> Tested-by: Sonny Sasaka <sonnysasaka@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: Fix init order in BT splitter Splitter needs to be inited BEFORE bluez thinks chip is, because some of what bluez does to bring chip up already needs splitter's intervention. This small patch makes sure that the splitter properly intervenes in the chip init to prevent the case of the init path already enabling LE. CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: make splitter switchable Adds a sysfs file that can be used to enable or disable HCI splitter. By default the splitter is in an uninitialized state where it will allow nobody access to the bluetooth chip. It can be once per boot moved to an enabled or a disabled state by writing to a sysfs file which can be found at /sys/devices/virtual/misc/hci_le/le_splitter_enabled. The acceptable values to write are standard kernel sysfs boolean values, eg "Y" or "yes" or "1", etc... Once a transition to one of the states happens, any further attempts to make another one will be denied. The current state can be read out of the same file and will always report "NOT SET
", "ON
", or "OFF
". Since bluez will be mightily confused about not being able to talk to the chip at boot, it will give up on it. So after moving to the enabled or disabled state, it is advised to kill and restart the userspace bluetoothd daemon, and then tell the kernel to bring up the interface again via the command "hciconfug hci0 up" or its equivalent. With the splitter on, newblue can be run, and with the splitter off, bluez has access to LE and newblue will fail to initialize if such initilization is attempted. BUG=b:74813838 TEST=manual for all 3 states. all works as expected Change-Id: I47d09cc423407cdb239a2428bbcff59773ecf021 Signed-off-by: Dmitry Grinberg <dmitrygr@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1551949 Commit-Ready: Sonny Sasaka <sonnysasaka@chromium.org> Tested-by: Sonny Sasaka <sonnysasaka@chromium.org>

u2fd: Store secret and counter as protos Stores the data inside protos rather than as raw bytes, and wraps the protos in a container that includes a hash for integrity checking. The use of protos allows us to easily extend functionality, for example if we need to keep track of migrating the counter from cr50, or storing the key in an alternate format. autotest: add a package of Bluetooth LE HID sanity tests The sanity package name is bluetooth_AdapterLEHIDSanity.py. The test is written as a package of tests in order to reduce test time, since auto-test ramp up time per test is costy. Between each two tests, the method _cleanup_and_restart is called to restart both peer and DUT. The HID device type (e.g. mouse or keyboard) can be selected per test using this method. At the end of each test, the method _update_test_result is called to track test results. At the end of the package, _print_test_results is called to print a summary of the test results. The test package contains 3 tests at this point - _test_connect_disconnect_loop _test_mouse_reports _test_auto_reconnect Test command example: test_that --autotest_dir ~/trunk/src/third_party/autotest/files/ --args "chameleon_host=<IP Fizz>" <IP DUT> bluetooth_AdapterLEHIDSanity To setup nrf52 device, please refer to - src/third_party/autotest-private/nRF52/ble_app_hids/README BUG=chromium:949394 TEST=running the test on eve device Change-Id: If69152f50907faa4c4b1a154722c2d08b46b39b0 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1551975 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Tested-by: Yoni Shavit <yshavit@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shyh-In Hwang <josephsih@chromium.org>
